defectClusters.description: On the existing mounted iOS component, caller replacement updates context/base/max but clears the available stove seed. Both public cases display 0 items / 1500 g and Choose shared equipment with disabled cover and confirmation instead of seeded stove, 1 item / 2300 g and Ready for departure. Same-process replacement and exact input binding are verified; .onChange/reset code is in production source. This is a single observed reset/seed defect manifested across two cases; the precise SwiftUI closure/state mechanism was not proven.

Rendered disabled SwiftUI buttons are additionally dimmed: disabled fill visibly becomes #E4EBE5 in light or #2B3E33 in dark rather than fixed #C9D7CC / #456251, with muted labels also dimmed. Original-state images independently show the discrepancy; source uses intended palette inside PlainButtonStyle plus .disabled. Numeric iOS native color cells remain U. This is one presentation defect repeated across states/cases.

initial.title: Ridge expedition pack
notes: Packing order: place dense equipment close to your back and keep the route map reachable. Check the actual pack before departure. This planning card records the chosen shared equipment; it does not replace the group leader’s final equipment inspection.

Weather changes quickly along the exposed ridge. Keep the optional weather cover at the top of the bag when selected. The cover protects equipment from brief rain and is not a substitute for the overnight shelter required by this route.

Each listed weight is the total carried weight for one shared item. The base load already includes personal clothing, food and the filled bottle. Do not add those items a second time when discussing the displayed total with the group.

Before leaving the meeting point, check straps, buckles and the tent poles with another member of the group. Record any damaged equipment with the trip coordinator. Availability shown here comes from the caller and may change when a new trip request arrives.

The disabled primary in light mode and disabled read-only classification controls in dark mode receive a visible extra fade beyond the brief’s border fill and muted text roles. The primary appears much paler than the reference disabled primary; dark disabled labels and fills are substantially dimmer than the assigned roles. Source explicitly selects border/muted colors and then applies PlainButtonStyle with disabled, consistent with the observed additional framework treatment. This is an appearance defect, not a claim that unsupported native iOS color measurements became available.

initial.title: Collection condition review
notes: Inspect each object in the queue and record its condition before submitting the review. Stable means no follow-up category is needed. Needs care requires a category so that the collection team can direct the object to the appropriate conservator.

Surface care covers visible finish and surface concerns; structure covers the support or physical assembly. This review records a routing category only. It does not prescribe a treatment, authorize cleaning or replace inspection by the collection’s conservation staff.

Moving between queue rows keeps decisions already entered for other objects. Read-only objects show their supplied condition and cannot be edited. An optional object may remain pending; every required object must have a complete decision before submission is enabled.

A new review request replaces all local decisions and focuses the caller’s requested object, or the first object when that identifier is unknown. The summary always counts the current complete decisions and care follow-ups across the entire queue, including objects outside the inspector.
